chunks: And Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one sheep for two sheep and one egg for two eggs. He said:
There is no harm, so long as it is not something measured or weighed.

key_terms.الشَّاةِ: a sheep, mentioned as an item of exchange
key_terms.الْبَيْضَةِ: an egg, mentioned as an item of exchange
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange one sheep for two sheep or one egg for two eggs in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on unequal exchange in certain goods. It indicates that exchanging items like animals or eggs in unequal quantities is permissible when the items are not among those sold by measure or weight, which relates to the rules of riba.
